timeline.message:
[ML] Offload request to generic threadpool

buildTextStructureResponse can take a long time, presumably up to 25s,
and is currently blocking the transport thread for that amount of time.
Offloading the request to the generic threadpool will at least let the
transport thread handle other requests concurrently.

Fix #109100
timeline.author: Pat Whelan

timeline.body:
nit: we could make a more positive assertion that we're on exactly the threadpool we expect:

```suggestion
        assert ThreadPool.assertCurrentThreadPool(Names.GENERIC);
```
Our executor services already preserve the calling thread's context. OTOH it's not great to submit a bare runnable here, could we use `ActionRunnable#supply` instead?

timeline.body: No need for the try/catch, `executorService.execute` won't throw anything if you give it an `AbstractRunnable`. And anyway this whole thing is running in a try/catch further up the stack.

Drive by comment, shouldn't this also be done for the TransportFindField/MessageStructureAction? 

It seems the cause of this bug is: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/commit/c70956ac167908c111df33ccb845d5601f99cebc

So we should make sure all structure finders get off loaded to the generic thread pool.

timeline.body: Think my previous comment was lost somewhere - there's no need for a `try/catch` here since `runnable` is an `AbstractRunnable`, which means the executor will notify it of exceptions and rejections directly.

reply.body: You are correct, I completely missed the previous comment.

timeline.body: Likewise here, no rejection can be thrown.
nit: use `ActionListener.delegateFailureAndWrap` rather than a bare `ActionListener.wrap` that manually delegates failures like this.

timeline.body: Why isn't `TextStructExecutor` used in this class (`TransportFindFieldStructureAction`) just like in the other two classes (`TransportFindMessageStructureAction`, `TransportFindStructureAction`)?

reply.body: I'm assuming we will want to leave this in when we eventually delete `TextStructExecutor`, whereas in the other two classes we will not.  Do you think this is correct? Otherwise, I can use `TextStructExecutor` here too and the future-dev can replace this line with `ActionListener.complete`.
Good call, I think you're correct. LGTM!

timeline.body: I think it'd make more sense to assert this in the various supplier implementations. We're clearly on the `GENERIC` pool here (and it seems unlikely we'd accidentally break that in future) but the important thing is that each `buildTextStructureResponse` is expensive and it's much less obvious in those implementations which threads they're using, so much riskier that we move that work somewhere inappropriate in a future change.
LGTM2 but one more suggestion about assertion placement.
